title: Your Ultimate Spectator Guide to the 2026 Sanlam Cape Town Marathon
claims: The 2026 race day is 24 May, with 27,000 runners taking on 42.2 km.

The start is on Beach Road, Green Point at 0 km; wheelchair athletes start at 07:50 from the Stadium, the elite wave at 08:00, the AbbottWMM Age Group World Championship wave from Beach Road at 08:05, and the final wave at 09:06.
The finish is on Vlei Road, Green Point at 42.2 km, with the final cut-off at 15:50 and the first wheelchair athlete expected around 09:30.
The N2 off-ramp is at 6.5 km, Rondebosch at 15–17 km with an elite refreshment table at 15.5 km, and Rondebosch Common at 20–22 km.
Salt River Circle is at 26.7 km, Woodstock's Albert Road at 27–29 km, Darling Street at 30 km, the Company Gardens at 30.7–32.1 km and Long Street at 32.1–33.3 km.
Green Point Main Road is at 34.2 km, and the Sea Point promenade out-and-back runs from 36.3 to 41.4 km, with runners heading about 3 km along the coast before turning back.
The Company Gardens climb is described as the longest and steepest of the day.

Western Cape Train Service operates a special event train on 24 May with return trips costing R20; spectators can use the Southern Line, and runners can connect to the start via a free shuttle between Thibault and Stadium Stop.
